solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Lost blood, with internal pain, having turned white

indicators.note: with internal says the second piece sits inside the first

parts.note: to lose blood is to bleed, past tense bled
an ache is a dull pain

explanation.surface: A wounded patient lost blood, suffered pain and went pale.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bleached has been turned white by light or chemicals, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Countryside transport appears on hour

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece appearing on another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: a bus is a form of public transport

explanation.surface: A rural bus timetable says the service turns up on the hour.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australia and Africa, the bush is wild, uncultivated countryside away from towns.

clue.text: Worry as to her range of hearing

indicators.note: to worry something is to shake it about, as a dog does a bone, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone frets about how far their words carry to a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worry' reads as a verb of anxiety but works like a dog worrying a bone, shaking the letters of AS TO HER into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: Earshot is the distance within which a sound or voice can be heard.

clue.text: Remark about Mass and religious instruction

indicators.note: about says the first piece goes round the others

parts.note: a remark is a comment
M is the physics abbreviation for mass

explanation.surface: A priest's words about the Mass, given as religious teaching.
explanation.definitionFit: A commandment, such as one of the Ten, is a divine rule or instruction in religion.

clue.text: Development of eastern nation

parts.note: a nation is a state

explanation.surface: A news item about the growth of some country in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Development' suggests progress, but here it is a housing development.
explanation.definitionFit: A housing estate is a development: a planned area of homes built together.

clue.text: Reversible raincoats and fleece

indicators.note: reversible says the word for raincoats is turned the other way round

parts.note: macs, short for mackintoshes, are raincoats

explanation.surface: A clothing listing: coats that turn inside out, and a fleece jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fleece' looks like another garment beside the raincoats, but it is the verb: to swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: To fleece someone is to cheat them out of money, which is what a con or swindle does.

clue.text: Hands round this from time to time

definitions.text: Hands round this from time to time

parts.words: Hands round this from time to time
parts.note: the hands of a dial sweep round its face, moving from one time to the next

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hands round' suggests passing things out now and then; really the hands go round the face, and 'from time to time' is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A clock face has hands that turn round it, pointing to each time in turn.

clue.text: Mother to stay put and avoid work

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
to linger is to stay on in one place

explanation.surface: Mum stays at home on the sofa rather than doing her job.
explanation.definitionFit: To malinger is to pretend to be ill so as to dodge work or duty.

clue.text: Disorderly mob get right into dirty film

indicators.note: into says the letter for right is put inside the other piece

parts.note: scum is a dirty film on the surface of a liquid

explanation.surface: A rowdy crowd gets right into watching a filthy movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dirty film' poses as a smutty movie but is a layer of scum. A scrum is also a crush of people, not just rugby.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrum is a disorderly crowd of people pushing and jostling together.

clue.text: Oil found on site after turning layer of earth

indicators.note: after puts the oil behind the other piece
turning says the word for site is read backwards

parts.note: a site is a spot or place
taken as written

explanation.surface: Drillers strike oil on a site after turning over the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Topsoil is the uppermost layer of soil in which plants grow.

clue.text: Painkiller poor Cleopatra swallows in the morning

indicators.note: swallows says the scrambled name takes the morning letters inside it
poor says the name is in a bad state, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: a.m. means in the morning

explanation.surface: Unwell Cleopatra takes a pill first thing in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges the queen's name to PARACETOL, and 'swallows' places the morning abbreviation inside it, after PARACET.
explanation.definitionFit: Paracetamol (acetaminophen in the US) is a common over-the-counter pain relief drug.

clue.text: Sorrowful hater could be construed as such

indicators.note: could be construed says the word hater is to be seen as the result of the solution read as an instruction

parts.note: the organ of love followed by a word meaning smashed up is an anagram instruction whose result is the word hater

explanation.surface: A sad person reflects that a hater might be read as one too.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the solution as two words: the first is what you get by breaking up 'hater', and the second says how.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone deeply saddened, usually by loss or love gone wrong, is sorrowful in the extreme.

clue.text: Shoved guards in back, getting chastised

indicators.note: guards says the word for shoved stands round the other piece

parts.note: shoved means pushed

indicators.note: back says the little word is read in reverse

explanation.surface: Bouncers shoved someone, guards holding them in at the back, then told them off.
explanation.definitionFit: Being chastised means being scolded or penalised for wrongdoing, a synonym.

clue.text: DIY nut is disorganised and messy

indicators.note: disorganised says the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A home-improvement enthusiast is chaotic and leaves a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: A DIY nut is a fan of do-it-yourself home repairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Untidy and messy both describe a cluttered, disordered state.

clue.text: One antelope finally enters enclosure in period of cold

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: enters says that letter goes inside the enclosure

parts.note: a cage is an enclosure

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word antelope

explanation.surface: A zoo antelope is finally put in its pen during a cold spell.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice age is a long era when glaciers spread and the climate is very cold.

clue.text: A game involving contracts or contract

parts.note: contract bridge is the card game where players bid for contracts

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a card game built on contracts, or a contract itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contract' at the end is a verb, to shorten, not the bridge noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a text is to shorten it, making it contract in length.

clue.text: She wraps revolting peasant in bandage

indicators.note: wraps says the word she is put round the other piece

parts.note: Wat Tyler led the English Peasants' Revolt of 1381

explanation.surface: A nurse binds up a rebellious farm worker's wounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolting' means rebelling, not disgusting: Wat Tyler led England's Peasants' Revolt of 1381.
explanation.definitionFit: To swathe is to wrap something up in cloth or bandages, so it can mean bandage as a verb.

clue.text: Where ships are safe from rocks or heading for trouble

definitions.text: Where ships are safe from rocks
definitions.meaning: a vessel far from shallows and reefs is out ...
the idiom for being in serious difficulty

explanation.definitionFit: In deep water is literally sea too deep for rocks, and idiomatically being in serious trouble.

clue.text: First time staying in seaside Butlins

indicators.note: staying in says the letters are lodged inside the words seaside Butlins

explanation.surface: A first holiday at a seaside Butlins camp.
explanation.walkthrough: Butlins is a British chain of seaside holiday camps.
explanation.definitionFit: A debut is a first appearance or first performance.

clue.text: In centre of a motorway, I dithered at first

indicators.note: at first picks the opening letter of each of the words before it

explanation.surface: A driver stranded mid-motorway hesitated at first.
explanation.definitionFit: Amid means in the middle of or surrounded by, a preposition like the clue's phrase.

clue.text: Usual practice at home

parts.note: a habit is a usual practice

explanation.surface: Someone describes their customary routine at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at home' reads as one phrase, but 'at' is wordplay and 'home' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitat is the natural home or environment of an animal or plant.

clue.text: Sinful woman married first man

parts.note: Adam was the first man in Genesis

explanation.surface: A wicked woman wed the first man, a nod to Eden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sinful woman' suggests Eve with Adam, but the answer is a brothel-keeper.
explanation.definitionFit: A madam runs a brothel, so the word can describe a woman of immoral trade.

clue.text: Go out with some friend at eight

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An invitation to go out with a friend at eight o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: To go out with someone romantically is to see them, a synonym of courting.

clue.text: Erudite elder involved with law

indicators.note: involved says the letters are tangled together into a new order

explanation.surface: A learned senior figure is busy with legal matters.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone well-read has read widely and so is learned or scholarly.
